payload.title: Tree-sitter analysis engine
payload.description:
Add a tree-sitter analysis engine to the scanner that works the same way for every language. Decision 2 of the parent initiative.

## Scope

- `web-tree-sitter` (WASM) in the scanner, with a `.wasm` grammar per language. No native build step at install.
- A shared capture vocabulary that every language's query file maps onto: `@scope`, `@definition.function`, `@definition.class`, `@definition.parameter`, `@definition.variable`, `@definition.field`, `@reference`, `@import.source`, `@import.name`, `@type.annotation`, `@comment`, `@string`, `@call.callee`, `@call.argument`.
- A language-neutral engine over those captures: enclosing scopes, same-file declaration lookup, comment attachment, syntax kind of a position.
- A per-language pack: grammar, `queries.scm`, and a config for doc-comment placement (Python docstring vs. comment above), import-path resolution rules, and test/fixture path patterns.
- TypeScript/JavaScript and Python packs first. They differ enough in doc comments, imports, and type annotations to test whether the vocabulary holds.
- Suggested layout: `src/analyze/engine/`, `src/analyze/languages/<lang>/`.

## Out of scope

- Changing the existing per-language detectors. That is the later migration epic.
- Type inference, cross-file call resolution, package-import resolution.

## Done when

- The engine answers, for any file position in a TS or Python file: syntax kind, enclosing function and class with ranges, attached doc comment, and the same-file declaration of an identifier.
- A file with a syntax error still yields scopes and declarations for the parts that parse.
- Adding a third language requires no engine code change (demonstrated with a stub pack or a small third language).

## Evaluation

Deterministic specs in the scanner's feature and unit suites. Corpus evaluation starts in the epics that consume the engine.
